body:

Problem (short version): Implement myAtoi(string s), which converts a string to a 32-bit signed integer. Skip leading whitespace, handle an optional +/- sign, read the digits, clamp to [-2^31, 2^31 - 1]. The full statement and examples are on the LeetCode page.

title: Design a JWT-based authentication service
body:
How to answer: This is a system design discussion. Walk us through your reasoning at a high level — focus on trade-offs and decisions, not exhaustive detail. You can sketch pseudocode or an API shape, talk through it, or both.

Tool policy: Any tool is fine for this question — including ChatGPT, Claude, or anything else. We're more interested in your reasoning and the questions you choose to ask the tools.

Keep your spoken answer under 2 minutes.

────────────────────────────────────────

Design a JWT-based authentication service that supports issuing tokens, refreshing them, and verifying requests.

Requirements:
  - Users can log in with email and password
  - On successful login, the system returns:
      - an access token (short-lived)
      - a refresh token (long-lived)
  - Clients can use the refresh token to obtain a new access token
  - The system should provide a way to verify incoming requests using the access token
  - Users should be able to log out from a single device

Please walk through:
  1. API design (endpoints and request/response)
  2. Data model (what needs to be stored server-side)
  3. Token design (what goes into access/refresh tokens)
  4. End-to-end flows (login, refresh, verify, logout)
  5. Security considerations and trade-offs
